items.title: Palace Skateboard's Beijing Flagship Takes Its Cues From the Great Wall
items.summary:
Summary 

Palace Skateboards is opening a two-story flagship in Beijing's Taikoo Li Sanlitun, designed around the brickwork of the Great WallGlass bricks, backlit green onyx and Chinese rosewood fill the space, alongside a hand-painted porcelain vase, a Tri-ferg fountain and a custom pianoA Beijing-exclusive capsule of tracksuits, hoodies and T-shirts pairs Tri-ferg graphics with Chinese zodiac motifs

Palace Skateboards is opening its Beijing flagship in Taikoo Li Sanlitun, a 211.3-square-meter store that takes the Great Wall as its main reference. The design turns the landmark's repeating brick construction and sense of continuity into a series of materials and set pieces, filtered through the Tri-ferg graphics and tongue-in-cheek details Palace is known for .

The building materials carry most of the Great Wall reference. Glass bricks and stone floors recreate the pattern and texture of the wall's masonry, while the plinths throughout the store are clad in green onyx marble. Because the onyx is translucent, Palace can light it from behind the brickwork so that Tri-ferg and P-shaped signage glows through the stone. Rosewood rounds out the palette, adding a second nod to Chinese materials and craftsmanship.

The ground floor is laid out in an L shape, with a narrow entrance side that opens into a larger room. Just inside the door, Palace signage hangs from the ceiling, lit on both sides so it seems to float, and a mirrored back wall doubles the effect. The first object visitors see is a 2-meter blue-and-white porcelain vase in the traditional Chinese style, hand-painted…
items.t: Palace Skateboard's Beijing Flagship Takes Its Cues From the Great Wall

Summary 

The Innioasis Y2 Music Player revives classic tactile navigation with an iPod-style touch-sensitive scroll ringThe offline-only device skips streaming apps in favor of user-loaded MP3s, lossless FLAC files and audiobooksHardware features include a small color screen, expandable microSD storage and both wired and Bluetooth headphone support

The digital audio landscape is taking a calculated step backward as offline listening stages a cultural return, and the newly introduced Innioasis Y2 Music Player stands at the forefront of this shift. Arriving as a direct successor to the brand’s previous Y1 player, the dedicated digital audio player utilizes an iPod -style touch-sensitive scroll ring to navigate its menus. The release taps into a growing hardware niche for distraction-free, offline audio devices that deliberately revive the classic tactile interfaces popularized throughout the mid-2000s. Measuring just four inches tall and less than half an inch thick, the compact hardware centers its design around a small color screen positioned directly above the touch-sensitive ring, offering a customizable interface that allows users to change the display theme.

Rather than relying on moving parts, the navigation wheel does not physically spin. Users simply slide their thumb around the surface to scroll through lists, ultimately pressing the center of the ring to make a selection. The outer edges of the touch ring act as controls for going back, skipping tracks and pausing playback. To streamline the listening experience, dedicated volume buttons are located entirely on…

items.title: Jyodan and Amiide on Turning Noriko Kose’s “Still I Miss You” Into an Award-Winning Sampling Contest Track
items.summary:
Noriko Kose's "Still I Miss You" — a masterpiece famously sampled in Nujabes' iconic "Reflection Eternal" and cherished globally as part of the DNA of lo-fi and jazzy hip-hop — has been breathed new life. Released in October 2025, "Still I Miss You" is a piano instrumental created by Kose as a self-homage to that very song.

Using this track as their sampling source, Jyodan and Amiide took the grand prize in an official sampling contest co-hosted by Tribe (a sub-label of Hydeout Productions), SURF Music, and Hypebeast. Longtime collaborators who previously gained a core following as members of the hip-hop crew CIRRRCLE and who now operate out of Hawaii and London/Tokyo as solo artists and as the duo Otomodatchi, the pair crafted the track "but, I still miss U" out of respect for the original. While preserving Kose's beautiful piano melody, they elevated it into a new classic that bridges past, present, and future.

Loved by listeners since its digital drop in January 2026, the track will see a physical 7-inch vinyl release on Sunday, December 27. To mark this milestone, Hypebeast conducted an exclusive interview with the duo. They discussed the story behind their winning track, their musical backgrounds, their current cross-border creative resonance, and their vision for the future.

We wanted to convey that the story is still ongoing by inserting 'but' 

Hypebeast: Tell us about the production process for the winning track. How did you divide the work? 

Amiide (A): As soon as I heard the original track we were sampling, I made a beat and sent it to Jyodan, saying, "Try…

items.title: Apple Captures 57% of US Smartphone Shipments in Q3 2026
items.summary:
Summary 

Apple captured 57% of the US smartphone market in Q3 2026 despite a broader industry downturnRising memory costs squeezed competitors and heavily impacted the low-end Android segmentSamsung emerged as the only major Android brand to grow its market share during the quarter

Apple dominated the domestic hardware scene in the third quarter of 2026, capturing 57% of all US smartphone shipments . According to a Counterpoint Research report released on November 26, 2026, Apple grew its market share from 50% the previous year even as overall US smartphone shipments fell 9% year-over-year. The company stood as the only major smartphone maker to avoid a year-over-year decline in shipment volume during the quarter.

This market share surge highlights a structural advantage for Apple when navigating component shortages and rising costs. While elevated memory costs squeezed the broader Android segment and forced competitors to raise prices, Apple kept iPhone pricing largely stable before releasing the iPhone 18 Pro lineup in September. Absorbing economic friction without passing the immediate burden onto consumers effectively weaponized Apple’s supply chain against rivals. Rising memory costs hit low-end Android smartphones particularly hard during the third quarter, turning an industry-wide supply issue into a competitive edge for the iOS ecosystem.

Samsung managed to carve out a localized victory amidst the broader Android struggle. The South Korean company was the only major Android smartphone maker to increase its shipment share, gaining one percentage point to capture…
items.t: Apple Captures 57% of US Smartphone Shipments in Q3 2026

items.title: Ford Goes Like Hell Again With the Le Mans-Bound GT41 Hypercar
items.summary:
Summary 

Ford unveils the GT41 with a Zack Snyder film narrated by Matt Damon.Standing 41 inches tall, it pairs a 5.4-liter V8 with hybrid power.Racing starts in Qatar in March 2027 before Le Mans in June.

Ford Racing has officially unveiled the Ford GT41, the all-new Hypercar spearheading its 2027 return to the top class of the FIA World Endurance Championship (WEC) and the 24 Hours of Le Mans . Making its public debut at Detroit’s Ford Field during the Thanksgiving Day clash between the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears, the GT41 arrives 60 years after the marque’s historic 1966 1-2-3 Le Mans sweep.

To celebrate the occasion, Ford tapped Zack Snyder and Matt Damon to create a cinematic anthem film. Shot in and around Los Angeles, the film tracks the GT41 being loaded into a shipping container bound across the Atlantic for Circuit de la Sarthe. Nodding to its heritage, the loading scene takes place inside the same hangar featured as the GT40 race workshop in Ford v Ferrari, with Damon, who portrayed Carroll Shelby in the film, lending his voice to narrate the next chapter of Ford’s enduring legacy.

Named as a direct successor to the four-time Le Mans-winning GT40 , the GT41 derives its name from standing 41 inches tall from the ground to its air intake. Beneath its blue-on-blue reveal livery, accented with hidden motifs of the American flag, a bald eagle, and Detroit’s “The Spirit of Detroit” sculpture, sits a 5.4-liter naturally aspirated Coyote-based V8 paired with a hybrid system. Its development draws directly from Ford’s Formula 1 partnership with Red Bull.…
items.t: Ford Goes Like Hell Again With the Le Mans-Bound GT41 Hypercar

items.title: Rockstar Developers Detail the 'GTA VI' Features That Got Cut
items.summary:
Summary 

Rockstar North developers revealed in an interview with German outlet 'PC Games' that several planned 'GTA VI' features were scrapped during developmentTennis, cinema and theater visits, crawling, home decorating and crafting were all considered before being droppedThe reasons ranged from quality concerns to features that didn't fit the game's story or felt too passive

Grand Theft Auto VI arrived with a long list of activities across Leonida, but Rockstar has now confirmed that several more were dropped before launch. In an interview with PC Games during the review period, Rockstar North development manager Rob Nelson and design producer Scott Mitchell went through the mechanics and pastimes that were planned for Jason and Lucia and didn't make the final game.

The biggest cut is tennis. The sport was a playable side activity in GTA V and was planned for its sequel, but according to the developers, Rockstar was never happy enough with how it played to ship it. Mini golf, on the other hand, made it into the final game, so Leonida still has at least one leisure sport.

Movie and theater outings were removed for a different reason. A cinema visit or a night at the theater was considered as a way to fill downtime, but Rockstar decided these were too passive. In a game built around player control, sitting and watching apparently didn't give players enough to do.

A third group of cuts dealt with how the two protagonists move through and live in their world. The team looked at letting Jason and Lucia crawl along the ground, decorate their homes and craft items. The…
items.t: Rockstar Developers Detail the 'GTA VI' Features That Got Cut

items.title: Toyota Turns Its Workhorse Into a Showstopper With the Hilux Hyper Z Prototype
items.summary:
Summary 

Toyota debuts the Hilux Hyper Z Prototype, inspired by Thailand’s custom truck scene.The bedless build features a racing cabin, towering wing, and 22-inch wheels.Strictly a design study, no production version expected.

Toyota has unveiled a radical interpretation of one of its vehicles with the Hilux Hyper Z Prototype. Developed by Toyota Design Australia from an idea first explored in 2024, the build introduces a slammed, motorsport-inspired silhouette atop the new Hilux Travo Z Edition as a nod to Thailand’s custom pickup scene.

Toyota overhauls the truck’s proportions and turns it into a wide, track-inspired machine. Measuring 5,360 mm long, 2,203 mm wide, and just 1,513 mm tall on a 3,085-mm wheelbase, the Hyper Z pairs a contrasting black hood and roof with white bodywork, swollen fenders, and thick black side skirts. A honeycomb lower grille spelling out “HILUX” sits above a low front splitter, while 22-inch wheels wrapped in 325/35 R22 Pirelli P Zero tires wear white aero covers lined with Toyota lettering. Inside the cabin, it’s thoroughly motorsport-inspired, featuring a roll cage, black racing seats and digital gauges.

In order to accommodate the towering rear wing, the Hyper Z eliminates both its tailgate and cargo bed, and added a sculpted black aero tray with illuminated “HILUX” lettering. Working alongside a front splitter, ground-effect underbody, and honeycomb rear diffuser, the wing helps manage airflow and cooling. Additional notable details include vertical LED taillights, “Hyper Z” rear fender graphics, and a “98 Hilux Prototype” door…
items.t: Toyota Turns Its Workhorse Into a Showstopper With the Hilux Hyper Z Prototype

items.title: Madhappy x Disney Launches a New Collection Inspired by Vintage Archives

Drawing on vintage graphics from the Disney archives, the collection reimagines artwork of Mickey Mouse, Pluto, and the rest of the "Mickey & Friends" crew through Madhappy’s signature color palettes and silhouettes.

The extensive lineup spans knits, fleeces, sweats, T-shirts, and headwear. Standout pieces boldly incorporate character graphics, featuring a Mickey Mouse knit bomber jacket and jogger pants accented with star patterns, alongside a zip-up knit showcasing both Mickey and Pluto. The collection also includes fleece zip-ups and sweatpants highlighting Mickey's various expressions, heart-motif hoodies, and ringer tees, while Pluto takes center stage on his own dedicated zip-ups and straight-leg sweatpants.

Rounding out the offering are Mickey Mouse knit polos and lightweight cardigans, logo-emblazoned heavyweight T-shirts, and character-adorned caps. The result is a collection that perfectly marries Disney’s nostalgic visuals with Madhappy’s core philosophy of optimism.

items.title: TOGA Drops Limited-Edition Sweatshirts Reimagining Champion's Reverse Weave
items.summary:
TOGA, the label helmed by Yasuko Furuta, has unveiled an exclusive collection with American athletic wear brand Champion. The release features two styles—a crewneck sweatshirt and a hoodie—that take the authentic silhouette of Champion’s signature Reverse Weave as their base, updated with boldly printed, colorful TOGA logos.

Reverse Weave is Champion’s proprietary construction method that prevents vertical shrinkage by cutting the fabric on the cross-grain rather than the standard vertical grain, while utilizing expansion gussets on the sides to manage horizontal shrinkage. For this special collaboration, the pieces retain these functional details while introducing TOGA's original cropped-length pattern exclusively for the size small, bringing a unique silhouette and fresh proportions to an everyday staple.

Available in three colors—gray, navy, and black—the crewneck sweatshirt retails for 26,400 yen and the hoodie for 28,600 yen. Both styles come in sizes S, M, L, and XL. A pre-sale kicks off at TOGA ISETAN SHINJUKU on Wednesday, December 2. The collection will then officially launch on Friday, December 4, at TOGA standalone boutiques, the label's official online store , and Rakuten Fashion . (*All prices include tax.)

items.title: A.P.C. x Native Union Want You to Pick Up the Phone Again
items.summary:
Summary 

A.P.C. and Native Union have teamed up on a tech accessory collection made for both outfits and everyday useThe standout piece is a retro phone handset that plugs straight into a smartphone over USB-C, with no pairing or charging neededA magnetic leather wallet and an iPhone case in Hazelnut leather complete the lineup

A.P.C. and Native Union have released a collaborative tech collection led by the POP PHONE, a handset styled after an old-school telephone receiver that turns a modern smartphone into something closer to a landline. Two leather pieces for the iPhone join it: a magnetic wallet and a protective case. Together they bring A.P.C.'s pared-back look to the gadgets people carry every day.

The partnership makes sense on paper. Native Union was founded in 2009 and has built its catalog around accessories for iPhone , AirPods and iPad, with an emphasis on function, new ideas and good materials. A.P.C. adds its signature restraint, and the result is a set of objects meant to work as finishing touches on an outfit as much as tools.

The POP PHONE is the most technically interesting piece. It plugs straight into a phone's USB-C port, so there is no battery to charge, no pairing and no Bluetooth to set up: you connect it and start talking. Inside are a high-quality microphone and speaker, plus built-in buttons to start and end calls and adjust the volume. The grip is shaped for long conversations, and the handset works with video call apps like Zoom, Teams and FaceTime. It isn't limited to phones either, since any tablet or laptop with a USB-C port can use it.…
items.t: A.P.C. x Native Union Want You to Pick Up the Phone Again

items.title: The Nike Mind 001 Sets Its Moving Nodes in Chocolate Brown for "Palomino"
items.summary:
Name: Nike Mind 001 “Palomino”
 Colorway: Palomino/Tar-Metallic Platinum
 SKU: HQ4307-201
 MSRP: $95 USD
 Release Date: Spring 2027

The Nike Mind 001 "Palomino" is set to give one of Nike's more experimental silhouettes an earthy update, with a palette built from olive, brown and flashes of metallic platinum. According to early details, the build is focused on how the shoe connects you to the ground, and Nike frames the design around feeling every surface and staying aware of each step.

From the side, olive does most of the work. It covers much of the profile and continues down to the wavy edge of the sole, while brown tones take over higher on the upper. A perforated panel in light brown runs from the collar almost to the toe and carries a small metallic silver Swoosh in its center. A second Swoosh stands upright on the outside of the molded shell for a bolder branding moment.

The outsole is where the Mind 001 stands apart. Twenty-two chocolate brown nodes are spread across the bottom, and each one moves on its own as you walk, so the sole adjusts to whatever is under it instead of acting as one rigid platform. That setup is central to Nike's pitch for the shoe, which centers on ground feel and a more deliberate stride.

Nike also adds a playful detail inside. The footbeds don't match: one carries "Nike Mind" in white lettering, and the other reads "Mind Science Department," which points back to the research-lab theme behind the line.

items.title: Panini Turns ‘GTA VI's’ In-Game Collectibles Into a Real Sports Trading Card Collection
items.summary:
Summary 

Panini America and Rockstar Games are releasing the ‘GTA VI’ Sports Trading Card Collection, their first trading card tie-in for the gameThe officially licensed set turns the collectible cards found inside ‘GTA VI’ into physical cardsParallels range from Special Silver, Pink, Teal and Light Blue up to numbered Legend Bronze, Silver and 1-of-1 Gold cards

Panini America and Rockstar Games are launching the GTA VI Sports Trading Card Collection, a licensed set that takes the card collectibles players chase in Grand Theft Auto VI and puts them into physical packs. It's the first trading card partnership built around the game, so collectors can open real packs of the same cards that show up in-game .

Each box holds four packs and is built to give a predictable spread of base hits. On average, a box yields two Rookies, one Retro and one Illustrated card, plus four Special Silvers, so every rip covers the set's main card styles. With the Rookies, Retros and Illustrated cards working as distinct subsets, collectors have a clear checklist to work through before the parallel hunt begins.

The parallels are where the chase gets serious. Beyond Special Silver, the set comes in Pink, Teal and Light Blue versions for collectors building rainbows. The numbered tiers then narrow quickly: Legend Bronze is limited to 49 copies, Silver drops to 25, and the Gold parallels are true 1-of-1s, making them the hardest cards in the set to pull.

The GTA VI Sports Trading Card Collection from Panini America and Rockstar Games is set to release in December 2026.

items.title: They’re bringing sexy back – but this time it’s classy | Jess Cartner-Morley
items.summary:
From a V-neck sweater worn back-to-front to a perfectly framed collarbone – here’s the secret to low-stakes sex appeal

I’m not sure when it started being not chic to want to look sexy, but it’s definitely a thing and it bothers me as it doesn’t feel truthful to the human experience, if that’s not a lot for the first sentence of a fashion column. Our wardrobes have become shrines to good taste. Well-cut coats and quality knitwear, elegant flat shoes and crisp white shirts. These clothes are excellent at communicating that you have read the briefing notes for the meeting and have some Booker prize chat. They are less good at suggesting you might be up for dancing on a table later.

Why do we have to choose? Clothes have always been partly about how they make us feel physically. We accept that an outfit can make you feel powerful, cool, smart. Why shouldn’t it also make you feel hot and fun?

items.title: Children of the revolution: how the north of England is defining modern men’s fashion
items.summary:
Once the historic centre of the textile industry, the north is now home to a host of a provenance-driven labels. But is there a specific northern menswear look? And what does it all mean for the mad-fer-it stereotypes?

In 2026, clothing has proved more important to Andy Burnham’s political identity than that of any British prime minister since Margaret Thatcher. He is a loyal Clarks and Adidas wearer, whose Howick worker’s jacket hangs in Manchester’s People’s History Museum. His ousting of Keir Starmer – launched shortly before being photographed jogging in a replica Everton shirt – has been memorialised as the “casual coup”. In one telling, the reason for this is simple: he’s a man from the north.

That Burnham is the first born-and-bred northern male PM since Harold Wilson last swished his Gannex raincoat out of Downing Street goes some way to explaining his higher interest in clothing. It’s not necessarily that all men in the south care less about clothing, or that all men in the north do – but that many men from the north express it in such a distinctive, even unified, way.

items.title: Brioche armchairs, butter sculptures and edible chandeliers: meet the new food artists
items.summary:
Culinary artists are turning fashion shows and design fairs into a feast for the eyes

A pretty Venetian chandelier featuring delicate pink flowers and cascading blue leaves hangs from a ceiling. A hazy, warm light radiates from its tulip bulbs. Suddenly, a woman reaches up and snaps off one of the flower stems, giggling as she begins to nibble it. Welcome to the weird and wonderful world of Laila Gohar. The Egyptian-born, New York-based artist is part of a new wave of culinary artists blurring the lines between sustenance and spectacle, and this troupe have quickly become a firm fixture at fashion parties and design fairs, turning dining into a phenomenon and delight.

Gohar describes the chandelier, made entirely from hand-spun sugar (including the silver chain that suspended it) as her “favourite thing she has done in recent history”. It joins a long list of extravagant yet still edible installations she has created, including lifesize armchairs made of brioche, an entire room constructed with Belgian chocolate and a four-metre-long mortadella that had to be lifted into the party’s venue using a crane.
